subject: na.rm=TRUE not respected within summarize for some variables

messages.author: 18636d58f7894a34
messages.subject: na.rm=TRUE not respected within summarize for some variables
parts:
I have encountered a situation where na.rm=TRUE for mean() is not respected within summarize. The following example illustrates the issue using a portion of a larger data file. When I recreate the data file by hand there is no problem. Am I missing something here?
## testNARM.R 
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)

origData <- import("https://www.dropbox.com/s/g2pw8eljoc8lh72/origData.RData?raw=1")

print(origData)

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using Ct")
checkMissing <- origData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(Ct, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

## na.rm not respected.
print("Missing using ex")
checkMissing <- origData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(ex, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()


## Re-create the data by hand.
byHandData <- tibble(sampleNumber=as.integer(c(33,34,35,36)),
                   genotype=factor(c("WT","WT","Casp1","Casp1"),
                     levels=c("WT","Casp1","Sluggish","control")),
                   condition=c(rep("none.PIC.18",4)),
                   gene=factor(c("Ef1a.2","Ef1a","Ef1a.2","Ef1a")),
                   Ct=c(NA, 7.420775, 7.685127, NA),
                   ex=c(NA, 1.0121389, 0.9831145, NA))
print(byHandData)

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using Ct")
checkMissing <- byHandData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(Ct, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using ex")
checkMissing <- byHandData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(ex, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()
